Subject: POC: Acme Health - Trial planning & workload intake

Hi Sofia — thanks again for taking the time earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC scoped and scheduled.

Call recap (what we heard)
- Goal: validate Redwood inference for Acme Health's clinical summarization pipeline and measure cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Success criteria suggested on call: >= 95% throughput match to baseline (within 10% token-level recall), 99th percentile latency < 800ms for typical requests, and cost < $0.02 per 1k tokens for production-like traffic.

Proposed evaluation plan
1) Workload intake: we need RPS, typical/90th/99th token lengths, concurrency, and burst patterns (see bullets below).
2) Short staged POC (2 weeks): smoke tests (3 days), scaled soak (7 days), regression/quality checks (4 days).
3) Success sign-off: technical + product (Acme) + Redwood.

Immediate asks (can you please provide):
- A sample traffic summary or CSV with timestamps + token counts (avg/max).
- Typical RPS and peak RPS (per minute).
- Expected concurrency (number of simultaneous in-flight requests).
- Any long prompt scenarios (avg and max token lengths).
- Preferred POC start window (we suggested 6/20 earlier).

Ownership & timeline
- Redwood PM / lead: Dylan Brooks (me) — orchestration and schedule.
- Redwood technical lead: Ben Carter — test config & capacity planning.
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole — success criteria and rollout plan.

If you can send the traffic CSV and any sample logs, Ben will use those to propose instance / batch sizing and an initial SOW.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this scheduled.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[dylan.brooks@redwood.com]

Thanks Dylan — appreciate the clear recap.

Attached is a short traffic summary (CSV) and a sample of anonymized request logs. Quick answers inline to your asks:
- Steady-state RPS: ~5 requests/sec.
- Peak RPS: ~40 requests/sec (bursts ~1-2 minutes, 1-2x per hour).
- Typical concurrency: 8-12 concurrent requests during peak; baseline is ~4-6.
- Token lengths: average prompt+completion ~120 tokens, 90th pct ~420, occasional outliers up to ~800 tokens for batch summaries.
- Preferred start window: week of Jun 20 looks good; procurement will need the SOW and MSA.

We do have PII considerations — logs are already de-identified but we'll need confirmation about how long logs are retained during the POC. Also looping in procurement contact (will forward separately).

Attachment: acme_traffic_summary.csv (text/csv), acme_sample_logs.json (application/json)

Hi all — reviewed the sample logs. Initial technical intake/questions and recommendations below.

Technical intake (please confirm / provide):
- Average payload size (bytes) and distribution (if available).
- Expected warm-up pattern (do you ramp traffic or cold start bursts?).
- KV-cache usage: are you using prefix caching or user-session caching?
- Any multi-turn state kept per user?
- Authentication/ingress: will you provide a VPN/VPC peering or will calls come from public IP ranges?

Observed from sample logs (assumptions):
- Avg tokens: ~120 (matches Sofia), 99th ~780
- Burst profile: short spikes to 40 RPS for 1-2 minutes; average 5 RPS
- Concurrency target for soak: 10 concurrent requests

Initial config proposal (starter profile)
- Model: open-variant-medium (quantized 4-bit for cost)
- Instance: 2 x A10G equivalent nodes for POC with autoscale to 4 nodes on sustained spikes
- Batching: dynamic batching target 25-40ms batch window; max batch size 64 tokens-equivalent
- KV-cache: recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts to reduce cost

POC timeline (technical run)
- Smoke tests: Jun 20-22
- Scale soak: Jun 23-29 (sustain concurrency 8-12)
- Quality/regression checks: Jun 30-Jul 3

Next steps
- Sofia: confirm payload sizes and whether you'd like Redwood to provision a VPC endpoint for the POC.
- Acme procurement: we need SOW + MSA signed to start provisioning.

Attachments (for reference): sample_batching_config.yaml (text), POC_SOW_v1.pdf (draft)

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC: Acme Health - Trial planning & workload intake

Thanks Ben — answers below and attaching the logs you requested.
- Average payload size: ~2.5KB per request (JSON payload).
- Warm-up: traffic is bursty; we see short cold spikes (1-2 mins) followed by return to baseline. Suggest Redwood provision for burst headroom.
- KV-cache: we use prefix caching for repeated prompts within a session (~70% cache hit for summaries).
- Multi-turn state: minimal, session scoped but not large (kept in our front end).
- Ingress: calls will originate from Acme public IP ranges; we can provide a static set for whitelisting.

Procurement / legal: looping in our procurement lead — Liam O'Connor (liam.oconnor@acmehealth.com). He will expect a short SOW + MSA.

Attached: acme_sample_logs.json (application/json)

Sofia
